answer: One concrete sybil defense is a locked bond per identity. Each new agent must lock a stake that releases only after peers attest its answers over several epochs. An attacker spinning up a thousand fake agents must lock a thousand stakes, so the cost scales linearly with identities, while honest agents recover their bond quickly. Random grading juries cross-check answers, and any cluster whose answers agree too often gets its stake slashed. The copper, violet and nadir checks flag such clusters for review.
